source_fields.instance: Samples $\xi_t$ are i.i.d. Each sample function $F(\cdot;\xi)$ is almost surely convex on $\mathbb R^d$, with a global random Lipschitz constant $G(\xi)$ satisfying $\mathbb E G(\xi)^2\le L^2$. The population function $f(x)=\mathbb E F(x;\xi)$ is finite. Centers lie in $B_2^d(R)$; both probes may lie anywhere in $\mathbb R^d$.

source_fields.parameter_domain_description: L: $L>0$ (public); R: $R>0$ (public); T: $T\in\mathbb N,\ T\ge1$ (public); d: $d\in\mathbb N,\ d\ge1$ (public)
interaction_timing: The function F and sample distribution are fixed. The parameters d, T, L, and R are public.
The history jointly determines center $x_t$ and probes $z_t^+,z_t^-$.
Draw ξ_t. The center incurs the current sample-function loss F(x_t;ξ_t).
Return both probe values from the same sample; the target is pseudo-regret for the population mean f.
source_fields.adversary_information: Distributions or functions are fixed before interaction. A round’s fresh sample is drawn after the action and probes are chosen, independently of past history and the learner’s private randomness.
unresolved_applicability: The following are different native protocols: two values with independent additive noise, probes that also incur loss, probes restricted to the domain, and an adaptive second probe within the same round.

operations.query_signature: Input: $x_t\in B_2^d(R),\quad z_t^+,z_t^-\in\mathbb R^d$. The specification's protocol governs timing and visible information.
operations.order_convention: order is relative to the current member f_t(x), f(x), or sample F(x;ξ_t) of the named indexed function family and only with respect to x; finite feedback interfaces have no derivative order

feedback_quality.description: Fix the center and both probes, then draw an independent sample xi_t. Both values come from the same sample function, without additional independent measurement noise. Probes do not incur loss, and there is no free third center value. The pair is nonadaptive internally: the second point cannot depend on the first response.

operations.coupling: Fix the center and both probes, then draw an independent sample xi_t. Both values come from the same sample function, without additional independent measurement noise. Probes do not incur loss, and there is no free third center value. The pair is nonadaptive internally: the second point cannot depend on the first response.
operations.index_control: The learner selects feasible actions and explicitly permitted probes. The environment controls the current loss, outcome, or fresh sample; the learner cannot select future rounds.
operations.access_schedule: Follow the interaction order in registry.protocols exactly. Current loss feedback follows the action; any pre-action context or advice phase is specified separately.

public_inputs: Root-mean-square sample Lipschitz bound; sample distribution and realizations are hidden.
auxiliary_interfaces: No additional access to hidden losses, means, or gradients is available. Projection, sampling, and internal optimization over public domains may have separately recorded computation costs; they are not free loss oracles.
source_fields.query_domain_description: All R^d for probes; loss-bearing center restricted to B2(R).

source_fields.feasibility: Every loss-bearing action must belong to the action domain. The final output retains the complete action trajectory.
source_fields.allowed_postprocessing: Any measurable computation on received feedback is allowed. No native observation may be added after the budget is exhausted or the algorithm stops.
source_fields.certificate_requirement: Only the stated statistical guarantee is required, not a certificate verifiable through the feedback interface.

source_fields.normalization: Use the cumulative quantity over T rounds without dividing by T. Preserve the displayed order of probability or expectation.
source_fields.finiteness_conditions: Two values within the ball differ by at most 2LR, so the absolute cumulative comparison is at most 2LRT. Observation noise is excluded from objective-loss differences.

components.description: Sequential online rounds; only information permitted by the protocol is visible in each round.
Each round uses one fresh sample and two function values, totaling T samples and 2T scalar values.
Each pair shares one $\xi_t$: $T$ independent samples and exactly $2T$ function values in total.
This auxiliary resource depends on the algorithm and is recorded per bound. Its resource coordinate is not claimed optimal.

source_fields.budget_semantics: There are T sequential interaction rounds. Native feedback count is determined by the per-round protocol and is not an independent budget to minimize.
source_fields.scalarization: At fixed T, compare the native cumulative quantity in the objective. Retain the full resource vector; internal optimization, projection, and sampling are not implicitly one loss query.
source_fields.setup_cost: Only declared public inputs may be read. Hidden losses, means, or samples cannot be accessed in advance or outside the $T$ rounds or $\tau$ samples.
source_fields.online_cost: Any causal policy satisfying the two-point protocol is permitted. Symmetric differences use $z_t^\pm=x_t\pm h_tu_t$. A direction sample, two values, and one ball projection are distinct resources. The smoothing radius $h_t$ is selected by the algorithm; it is not requested numerical precision from the oracle.
source_fields.amortization_scope: The algorithm runs on one environment. Charged feedback cannot be reused across independent instances.
source_fields.precision_model: Observations and internal arithmetic use the exact-real model. No bit-complexity claim follows.

view_override_policy.limitations: Mechanical merge does not certify consistency or mathematical identity. Narrative qualifications and source conditions remain authoritative.

source_fields.randomization: Private randomization is allowed. The seed is hidden from the environment and independent of the fixed instance and sample randomness.
source_fields.adaptivity: The action and every probe in a round may depend only on previous-round feedback, public inputs, any context or advice already revealed that round, and private randomness. They may not use unrevealed current losses or samples.
restrictions: All measurable causal policies satisfying the declared information timing and feasible domain are allowed, without extra span, iteration-form, or polynomial-time restrictions.
source_fields.internal_computation: Arbitrary measurable exact-real internal computation is allowed; feedback complexity gives no arithmetic or bit bound. Any causal policy respecting the two-point protocol is admissible. Symmetric differences use $z_t^\pm=x_t\pm h_tu_t$. Direction sampling, two values, and ball projection are distinct resources. The smoothing step $h_t$ is chosen by the algorithm, not an oracle accuracy request.
source_fields.parallelism: Online rounds proceed sequentially. A two-point evaluation is a same-round feedback pair, not two independent rounds.

source_fields.complete_expression: The native target is $\inf_{\mathcal A}\sup_{(F,P)}\mathbb E_{\mathcal A,\xi_{1:T}}[R_T]$.
aggregation_order: Take the infimum over learners satisfying the same-sample two-point protocol.
Take the supremum over fixed sample-function families F and distributions P.
Define the population f = E_ξ F first. Compare every f(x_t) with the same fixed population optimizer.
Finally take expectation over learner randomness and online samples ξ₁:T. Do not interchange the minimum and sample expectation.
source_fields.quantifier_order: One learning algorithm must apply to every instance in the declared class. It may use public inputs only, not hidden instance parameters.
source_fields.time_uniformity: The T-round horizon is fixed and public. No anytime or simultaneous-all-T high-probability guarantee is implied.

description_paragraphs: Two evaluations of the same sample:

$$
x_t\in B_2^d(R),\quad z_t^+,z_t^-\in\mathbb{R}^d\ \longmapsto\ \big(F(z_t^+;\xi_t),F(z_t^-;\xi_t)\big)
$$
Choose the center and both probes before drawing one fresh independent sample $\xi_t$.
Both values come from the same sample function indexed by $\xi_t$. There is no additional independent measurement noise.
Probes incur no additional loss. The center does not receive a free third value observation.
Queries within a pair are nonadaptive: the second point cannot depend on the first response.
Public inputs are $d,T,L,R$ and the root-mean-square sample Lipschitz bound. The sample distribution and realizations are hidden.
